Actual Behaviour: Every question renders 12 choices at once. On 390x844 only part of the list fits and Next is multiple screens below; a full run requires scanning 144 labels.
Test Steps: Run the complete quiz at 390x844; inspect first, middle, and last questions; count choices and taps; verify selected state, progress, back navigation, result arrival, no horizontal overflow, and optional email boundary.
Test Result: FAIL — the mobile quiz is operable but too scan-heavy for the stated two-minute experience.
Error / Bug Found: Twelve simultaneously visible options per question create avoidable mobile cognitive and scrolling load.
Fix Implemented: Changed the simultaneous 12-option display into four accessible response disclosures with three visible choices, plain summaries, and sticky mobile controls.
Retest Steps: Repeat the persona walkthrough and all affected existing feature stories after any tracker-backed fix.
Retest Result: PASS — production exposes four response groups, one open group, three visible choices, and completes all 12 questions without horizontal overflow.
Notes: Evidence: qa_evidence/persona-audit/persona-retest-after.txt; qa_evidence/persona-audit/lighthouse-mobile-final.json
Original Prompt: Audit the MIRROR//LOOP website from several different user personas and improve it.

User Story: As a privacy-conscious visitor, I want to complete the reflection anonymously and understand any measurement that occurs, so that I remain in control of my information.
Expected Behaviour: The visitor can reach the result without email; concise privacy information is available before starting; analytics and email collection are explained in accessible language; no hidden form or challenge blocks anonymous completion.
Actual Behaviour: Anonymous completion and aggregate-only payloads pass, but the concise analytics disclosure is discoverable only through the footer privacy page.
Test Steps: Complete the quiz without email; inspect browser storage and network payloads; find privacy disclosure from the initial journey; verify the privacy notice distinguishes aggregate analytics from subscription data.
Test Result: FAIL — the visitor cannot learn about anonymous aggregate counting at the point of starting the quiz.
Error / Bug Found: The pre-start privacy promise omits the aggregate analytics behavior.
Fix Implemented: Added point-of-decision privacy copy and deferred third-party Turnstile loading until the optional email form appears after the result.
Retest Steps: Repeat the persona walkthrough and all affected existing feature stories after any tracker-backed fix.
Retest Result: PASS — initial production load makes only first-party requests; the pre-start copy explains optional email, in-browser choices, aggregate counts, and links to details.
Notes: Evidence: qa_evidence/persona-audit/persona-retest-after.txt; qa_evidence/persona-audit/production-route-and-copy-checks.txt

User Story: As a visitor using the reflection during a stressful moment, I want language that is nonjudgmental and actionable, so that the result supports reflection without defining or alarming me.
Expected Behaviour: Questions avoid shame and deterministic labels; the result explains strengths and limits in ordinary language; the suggested action is small and safe; the experience does not imply crisis, fate, pathology, or guaranteed transformation.
Actual Behaviour: Result language and action prompts are safe, but several question labels use ominous or pathologizing language during a potentially stressful reflection.
Test Steps: Read every question, all answer options, all 12 result summaries, and prompts through a psychological-safety lens; verify boundary language and check whether loaded labels are explained or softened.
Test Result: FAIL — Shadow Contracts, Pattern Collapse, destabilizes, and breaks are unnecessarily loaded for the public experience.
Error / Bug Found: Loaded system vocabulary can intensify rather than steady a vulnerable visitor.
Fix Implemented: Rewrote loaded question topics and selected answer labels in calm, ordinary language while preserving intent and scoring codes.
Retest Steps: Repeat the persona walkthrough and all affected existing feature stories after any tracker-backed fix.
Retest Result: PASS — public prompts no longer use the flagged ominous system terms, and all results retain non-diagnostic boundaries and small actionable prompts.
Notes: Evidence: qa_evidence/persona-audit/persona-retest-after.txt
Original Prompt: Audit the MIRROR//LOOP website from several different user personas and improve it.

Route / Screen / Command / Entry Point: Result, supporting pattern, retake, email offer
User Story: As a returning visitor, I want to understand the primary and supporting patterns and retake intentionally, so that I can compare reflections without mistaking them for permanent scores.
Expected Behaviour: The result explains why two patterns are shown, what each contributes, and what changes on retake; the visitor can retake without stale answers or mandatory subscription.
Actual Behaviour: Retake resets correctly, but the supporting pattern is an unexplained name; when all answers select one archetype, a zero-count archetype is still displayed as supporting because of deterministic tie-breaking.
Test Steps: Complete the quiz with a known answer sequence; assess whether primary and supporting pattern meanings are self-contained; retake with a different sequence; verify answers reset and result framing remains a current snapshot.
Test Result: FAIL — a zero-evidence supporting pattern can be shown, and nonzero supporting patterns receive no explanation.
Error / Bug Found: The supporting-pattern presentation overstates evidence and lacks interpretive context.
Fix Implemented: Added primary frequency, supporting-pattern explanation and frequency, and a zero-count safeguard; retained complete retake reset behavior.
Retest Steps: Repeat the persona walkthrough and all affected existing feature stories after any tracker-backed fix.
Retest Result: PASS — 7/5 production answers explain both patterns; 12/0 answers state that no second pattern stood out; retake resets all answer state.
Notes: Evidence: qa_evidence/persona-audit/persona-retest-after.txt
Original Prompt: Audit the MIRROR//LOOP website from several different user personas and improve it.

Route / Screen / Command / Entry Point: All production pages after a deploy
User Story: As a returning visitor, I want each deployed page to load mutually compatible code and styles, so that an update cannot leave me with a broken mixed-version experience.
Expected Behaviour: HTML references versioned app and style assets; app module imports are versioned together; a production reload after deployment exposes the new DOM behavior without requiring users to clear their browser cache.
Actual Behaviour: FAIL — after the first persona-improvement deploy, production served the new HTML while the browser reused the previous app.js; the expected response-group elements were absent.
Test Steps: Deploy changed HTML, CSS, app.js, and module dependencies; reload from an existing browser session; verify the new section labels, response-group elements, styling, and result behavior load as one release.
Test Result: FAIL — production reported section “Finding direction” from fresh quiz JSON but zero .response-group elements because cached app.js rendered the old fieldset implementation.
Error / Bug Found: Stable asset URLs permit a mixed release when Firebase or the browser caches JavaScript and CSS for up to one hour.
Fix Implemented: Added one release version to HTML stylesheet/config/app URLs and matching JavaScript module imports, then redeployed and verified the production DOM.
Retest Steps: Add one release version across HTML asset URLs and JavaScript module imports; redeploy; reload the existing browser session and verify all new elements and behaviors.
Retest Result: PASS — release 20260826-3 loaded version-matched CSS, config, app, and modules and exposed the expected progressive response-group DOM.
Notes: Evidence: qa_evidence/persona-audit/production-route-and-copy-checks.txt; qa_evidence/persona-audit/persona-retest-after.txt
Original Prompt: Audit the MIRROR//LOOP website from several different user personas and improve it.

User Story: As a confirmed subscriber, I want a supporting pattern shown only when my choices support it, so that the email does not invent a second result.

Actual Behaviour: PASS — Score now records deterministic counts and assigns a supporting pattern only when its count is greater than zero; email rendering enforces the same condition.
Test Steps: Score twelve identical answers and assert there is no supporting pattern; score a split answer set and assert the supporting code and count are deterministic; capture both reflection emails and verify conditional rendering.
